sections.h2: What a ticket is, and how it differs from a service call
paras: A ticket is the customer's side of the conversation. It starts when somebody at the hospital or the dealership has a problem or a question, and it ends when they agree it has been dealt with. Some tickets become field service calls. Many do not: a consumable query, a missing document, a training request, a billing question.

Aura Business runs this as the Ticketing and Helpdesk suite, with Ticket Management, a status workflow, internal notes, SLA timers, customer ticket submission from the portal and CSAT on close. Keeping it separate from dispatch matters, because a support desk that treats every query as an engineer visit either sends engineers unnecessarily or ignores everything that is not a breakdown.

sections.h2: When every query arrives as a phone call, nothing is ever finished.
sections.lead: Support that lives on calls and personal WhatsApp has no queue, no owner and no record, so the same question is answered three times and the difficult one is answered never.

items.q: Can our customers raise tickets themselves?
items.a: Yes. Customer ticket submission is part of the self-service portal, so a hospital's biomedical team can raise an issue with attachments at any hour and follow its status without ringing your office.

items.q: How is a ticket different from a service call?
items.a: A ticket is a customer request of any kind. A service call is an engineer visit. Tickets that need an engineer convert to a service call and go to dispatch. See service dispatch.

items.q: Can we control who sees internal notes?
items.a: Yes. Internal notes are for your team and are not shown in the customer portal view, while the status and the resolution are. Role-based access controls who can see and change what.
Yes. Where a contract sets response times, the timer runs on the ticket and at-risk tickets are flagged. See SLA management.
